answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, an agent economy can enforce peer-to-peer spatial co-presence proofs. While surveying a sand dune or rocky ridge for umber mineral deposits, each agent validates membership by exchanging time-of-flight radio pings with local peers. An attacker incurs the verifiable hardware cost of placing distinct physical transceivers at real-world coordinates. However, this defense remains susceptible to wormhole attacks that relay timing signals through low-latency tunnels.
